verses.sanskrit:
सञ्जय उवाच।
              तमब्रवीद्वासुदेवो रथस्थो राधेय दिष्ट्या स्मरसीह धर्मम् । प्रायेण नीचा व्यसनेषु मग्ना निन्दन्ति दैवं कुकृतं न तु स्वम् ॥१॥
verses.english: Sanjaya said Then Krishna, who was on the car said to Karna-"Fortunate it is, O son of Radha, that you remember virtue. It is always seen that men, when they are in distress, speak ill of the providence and not of their own evil deeds.

verses.sanskrit: यद्द्रौपदीमेकवस्त्रां सभायामानाययेस्त्वं च सुयोधनश्च । दुःशासनः शकुनिः सौबलश्च न ते कर्ण प्रत्यभात्तत्र धर्मः ॥२॥
verses.english: You, Duryodhana, Dushasana and Subala's son Shakuni, brought Draupadi, clad in one piece of cloth, before the court. Then O Karna, this virtue of yours, did not display itself.

verses.sanskrit: यदा सभायां राजानमनक्षज्ञं युधिष्ठिरम् । अजैषीच्छकुनिर्ज्ञानात् क्व ते धर्मस्तदा गतः ॥३॥
verses.english: When Shakuni, a clever hand at dice, defeated Kunit's son Yudhishthira who was innocent of the game where was this virtue of yours?

verses.sanskrit: वनवासे व्यतीते च कर्ण वर्षे त्रयोदशे । न प्रयच्छसि यद्राज्यं क्व ते धर्मस्तदा गतः ॥४॥
verses.english: When the period of exile and the thirteenth year (of concealment) was over and you did not return the Pandavas their kingdom where was his virtue of yours.

verses.sanskrit: यद्भीमसेनं सर्पैश्च विषयुक्तैश्च भोजनैः । आचरत्त्वन्मते राजा क्व ते धर्मस्तदा गतः ॥५॥
verses.english: When at your advice the Kuru king attempted to kill Bhima through snakes and poisoned food where was this virtue of yours?

verses.sanskrit: यद्वारणावते पार्थान्सुप्ताञ्जतुगृहे तदा । आदीपयस्त्वं राधेय क्व ते धर्मस्तदा गतः ॥६॥
verses.english: When you set fire to the wax-house at Varanavata for burning the sleeping Pandavas to death where was this virtue of yours?

verses.sanskrit: यदा रजस्वलां कृष्णां दुःशासनवशे स्थिताम् । सभायां प्राहसः कर्ण क्व ते धर्मस्तदा गतः ॥७॥
verses.english: When you laughed at Draupadi while she, spare dressed and in her season, stood before the court at Dusasana's will where was this virtue of yours?

verses.sanskrit: यदनार्यैः पुरा कृष्णां क्लिश्यमानामनागसम् । उपप्रेक्षसि राधेय क्व ते धर्मस्तदा गतः ॥८॥
verses.english: O son of Radha! Where your religion (rule) was slipped when you once observed Draupadi getting torture in the hands of mean Kauravas.

verses.sanskrit: विनष्टाः पाण्डवाः कृष्णे शाश्वतं नरकं गताः । पतिमन्यं वृणीष्वेति वदंस्त्वं गजगामिनीम् ॥९॥
verses.english: O Krishna, the Pandavas have been slain and are gone to eternal damnation; do you, therefore, O one of sweet voice and heavy posteriors, take to yourself another lord. Betake not to the service of Dhritarashtra as a maid, for, O lotus-eyed one, your husbands are no more (in the land of the living). O Krishna, this day forth the Pandavas will no longer have any control over you.

verses.sanskrit: उपप्रेक्षसि राधेय क्व ते धर्मस्तदा गतः । राज्यलुब्धः पुनः कर्ण समाह्वयसि पाण्डवान् ॥१०॥
verses.english: When you spoke to the Princess Draupadi, of dignified elephantine gait, “O Draupadi, the Pandavas are lost into eternal hell, choose another husband" and looked on the scene with glee where was this virtue of yours?

verses.sanskrit: यदा शकुनिमाश्रित्य क्व ते धर्मस्तदा गतः । यदाऽभिमन्युं बहवो युद्धे जघ्नुर्महारथाः । परिवार्य रणे बालं क्व ते धर्मस्तदा गतः ॥११॥
verses.english: When thirsting for the kingdom and relying on the king of Gandharas you invited the Pandavas to a game at dice where was this virtue of yours?

verses.sanskrit: यद्येष धर्मस्तत्र न विद्यते हि किं सर्वथा तालुविशोषणेन ॥१२॥
verses.english: If this your virtue, the aid of which you now solicit, was no where on all those Occasions what is the use of drying up your tongue by uttering that word? You now wish to practise virtue, O Suta, but you shall not escape with your life.

verses.sanskrit: अद्येह धर्म्याणि विधत्स्व सूत तथापि जीवन्न विमोक्ष्यसे हि । नलो ह्यक्षैर्निर्जितः पुष्करेण पुनर्यशो राज्यमवाप वीर्यात् ॥१३॥
प्राप्तास्तथा पाण्डवा बाहुवीर्यात्सर्वैः समेताः परिवृत्तलोभाः । निहत्य शत्रून्समरे प्रवृद्धान् ससोमका राज्यमवाप्नुयुस्ते ॥१४॥
verses.english: Like Nala who was vanquished by Pushkara at a game of dice, but who regained his kingdom by dint of his power, the Pandavas, who are free from cupidity, will regain their kingdom by the force of their arms and help of their friends. Having killed their powerful enemies they with the Somakas will regain their kingdom. The sons of Dhritarashtra will be killed by those best of men who are always shielded by virtues.

verses.sanskrit:
तथा गता धार्तराष्ट्रा विनाशं धर्माभिगुप्तैः सततं नृसिंहैः । सञ्जय उवाच।
              एवमुक्तस्तदा कर्णो वासुदेवेन भारत ॥१५॥
लज्जयावनतो भूत्वा नोत्तरं किञ्चिदुक्तवान् । क्रोधात्प्रस्फुरमाणौष्ठो धनुरुद्यम्य भारत ॥१६॥
verses.english: Sanjaya said Thus accosted by Krishna, O descendant of Bharata, Karna hung down his head in shame and made no reply.

verses.sanskrit: योधयामास वै पार्थं महावेगपराक्रमः । ततोऽब्रवीद्वासुदेवः फाल्गुनं पुरुषर्षभम् ॥१७॥
verses.english: With lips trembling in anger, he, of great energy and prowess, took up his bow and began to fight with Arjuna.

verses.sanskrit: दिव्यास्त्रेणैव निर्भिद्य पातयस्व महाबल । एवमुक्तस्तु देवेन क्रोधमागात्तदार्जुनः ॥१८॥
verses.english: Then Vasudeva's son said to Phalguna, that best of men-"Strike Karna down with a celestial weapon."

verses.sanskrit: मन्युमभ्याविशद्धोरं स्मृत्वा तत्तु धनञ्जयः । तस्य क्रुद्धस्य सर्वेभ्यः स्रोतोभ्यस्तेजसोर्चिषः ॥१९॥
verses.english: Thus accosted by the deity Arjuna was worked up with anger. And recollecting all the incidents Dhananjaya was possessed by a terrific rage.

verses.sanskrit: प्रादुरासंस्तदा राजंस्तद‌द्भुतमिवाभवत् । तत्समीक्ष्य ततः कर्णो ब्रह्मास्त्रेण धनञ्जयम् ॥२०॥
verses.english: Then, O king, as if scintillations of fire began to come put from the pores of the angry Partha's body. The scene was exceedingly wondrous.

verses.sanskrit: अभ्यवर्षत्पुनर्यत्नमकरोद्रथसर्जने । ब्रह्मास्त्रेणैव तं पार्थो ववर्ष शरवृष्टिभिः ॥२१॥
verses.english: Seeing it Karna invoked the Brahma weapon, shot arrows on Dhananjaya and tried once more to get rid of his car. arrOWS son

verses.sanskrit: तदस्त्रमस्त्रेणावार्य प्रजहार च पाण्डवः । ततोऽन्यदस्त्रं कौन्तेयो दयितं जातवेदसः ॥२२॥
verses.english: Partha, also, by his Brahma weapon made a down pour of upon Karna. Counteracting the arrows of his enemy with those of his own Pandu's son continued to strike him.

verses.sanskrit: मुमोच कर्णमुद्दिश्य तत्प्रजज्वाल तेजसा । वारुणेन ततः कर्णः शमयामास पावकम् ॥२३॥
verses.english: Then aiming at Karna Kunti's discharged another favourite weapon of his powerful as the fire.

verses.sanskrit: जीमूतैश्च दिशः सर्वाश्चक्रे तिमिरदुर्दिनाः । पाण्डवेयस्त्वसंभ्रान्तो वायव्यास्त्रेण वीर्यवान् ॥२४॥
verses.english: Karna, however, put out that fire with Varuna (watery) weapon. Suta's son covered all the directions with clouds created by his arrows and it appeared like a rainy day.

verses.sanskrit: अपोवाह तदाऽभ्राणि राधेयस्य प्रपश्यतः । ततः शरं महाघोरं ज्वलन्तमिव पावकम् ॥२५॥
verses.english: Then before the very presence of Karna, the powerful son of Pandu scattered those clouds with his Vayavya weapon.

verses.sanskrit: आददे पाण्डुपुत्रस्य सूतपुत्रो जिघांसया । योज्यमाने ततस्तस्मिन् बाणे धनुषि पूजिते ॥२६॥
verses.english: Then for killing the son of Pandu, the charioteer's son took up another dreadful arrows shining like the fire.

verses.sanskrit: चचाल पृथिवी राजन् सशैलवनकानना । ववौ सशर्करो वायुर्दिशश्च रजसा वृताः ॥२७॥
verses.english: When that arrow was set on the bow-string, O king, the earth shook with her mountains, watery expanses and forests.

verses.sanskrit: हाहाकारश्च सञ्जज्ञे सुराणां दिवि भारत । तमिषुं सन्धितं दृष्ट्वा सूतपुत्रेण मारिष ॥२८॥
verses.english: Violent winds blew scattering pebbles. All the directions were covered with dust and cries of lamentation arose amongst the celestials in the sky.

verses.sanskrit: विषादं परमं जग्मुः पाण्डवा दीनचेतसः । स सायकः कर्णभुजप्रमुक्तः शक्राशनिप्रख्यरुचिः शिताग्रः ॥२९॥
verses.english: Seeing that arrows aimed by Karna, the Pandavas were worked with depression and sorrow.

verses.sanskrit: भुजान्तरं प्राप्य धनञ्जयस्य विवेश वल्मीकमिवोरगोत्तमः । स गाढविद्धः समरे महात्मा विघूर्णमानः श्लथहस्तगाण्डिवः ॥३०॥
verses.english: The keen arrows, effulgent like Shakra's thunder-bolt shot off Karna's hands, fell upon Dhananjaya's breast and went into it like a serpent penetrating an ant-hill.

verses.sanskrit: चचाल बीभत्सुरमित्रमर्दनः क्षितेः प्रकम्पे च यथाऽचलोत्तमः । तदन्तरं प्राप्य वृषो महारथो रथाङ्गमुर्वीगतमुज्जिहीर्षुः ॥३१॥
verses.english: Thus wounded that chastiser of enemies, the high-souled Vibhatsu began to reel. His grasp became loosened and his bow Gandiva, dropped off his hands. He shook there like the king of mountain in an earth-quake.

verses.sanskrit: रथादवप्लुत्य निगृह्य दोर्भ्यां शशाक देवान्न महाबलोऽपि । ततः किरीटी प्रतिलभ्य संज्ञां जग्राह बाणं यमदण्डकल्पम् ॥३२॥
verses.english: During this opportunity the great carwarrior Vrisha leaped down from his chariot to extricate the wheel that had been sunk underneath the earth. Holding it with his two hands he tried his best of get it out. But unfortunately for his bad luck he failed through he was possessed of great strength.

verses.sanskrit: ततोऽर्जुनः प्राञ्जलिकं महात्मा ततोऽब्रवीद्वासुदेवोऽपि पार्थम् । छिन्ध्यस्य मूर्धानमरेः शरेण न यावदारोहति वै रथं वृषः ॥३३॥
verses.english: In the interval regaining his consciousness the diadem-decked and the high-souled Arjuna took his arrow Anjalika which was fatal as the rod of Death. Thereupon Krishna said to Partha-"Cut-off with this arrow the head of your enemy before he gets upon his car.”

verses.sanskrit: तथैव सम्पूज्य स तद्वचः प्रभोस्ततः शरं प्रज्वलितं प्रगृह्य । जघान कक्षाममलार्कवर्णां महारथे रथचक्रे विमग्ने ॥३४॥
verses.english: Praising highly those words of Lord Krishna and while the wheel of his enemy was still under the earth the great car-warrior Arjuna took up a highly effulgent, razorheaded arrow and struck down Karna's standard bearing the emblem of an elephant and shining like the spotless sun.

verses.sanskrit: तं हस्तिकक्षाप्रवरं च केतुं सुवर्णमुक्तामणिवज्रपृष्ठम् । ज्ञानप्रकर्षोत्तमशिल्पियुक्तैः कृतं सुरूपं तपनीयचित्रम् ॥३५॥
verses.english: That standard bearing the elephant was decorated with gold, pearls, gems and diamonds and was made with great skill by the best of artizans. It was highly beautiful and made of pure gold.

verses.sanskrit: जयास्पदं तव सैन्यस्य नित्यममित्रवित्रासनीड्यरूपम् । विख्यातमादित्यसमं स्म लोके त्विषा समं पावक-भानु-चन्द्रैः ॥३६॥
verses.english: That standard always used to inspire your soldiers with courage and fill your enemies with fear. Its form was highly praiseworthy. Known all over the world it was effulgent like the sun.

verses.sanskrit: ततः क्षुरप्रेण सुसंशितेन सुवर्णपुङ्खेन हुताग्निवर्चसा । श्रिया ज्वलन्तं ध्वजमुन्ममाथ महारथस्याधिरथेः किरीटी ॥३७॥
verses.english: With that keen, gold-winged razor, headed arrow effulgent like fire, fed with libations of clarified butter the diadem-decked Arjuna cutoff that standard of Adhiratha's son, the great car-warrior.

verses.sanskrit: यशश्च दर्पश्च तथा प्रियाणि सर्वाणि कार्याणि च तेन केतुना । साकं कुरूणां हृ‌दयानि चापतन् बभूव हाहेति च निःस्वनो महान् ॥३८॥
verses.english: With that standard fell the glory, pride, hope of success and everything dear unto the hearts of the Kurus. And cries of lamentations arose in your army.

verses.sanskrit: दृष्ट्वा ध्वजं पातितमाशुकारिणा कुरुप्रवीरेण निकृत्तमाहवे । नाशंसिरे सूतपुत्रस्य सर्वे जयं तदा भारत ये त्वदीयाः ॥३९॥
verses.english: Seeing that standard struck down by the light-handed Kuru hero your soldiers gave up all hopes of Karna's success.

verses.sanskrit: अथ त्वरन् कर्णवधाय पार्थो महेन्द्रवज्रानलदण्डसन्निभम् । आदत्त चाथाञ्जलिकं निषङ्गात्सहस्ररश्मेरिव रश्मिमुत्तमम् ॥४०॥
verses.english: Then wishing to kill Karna quickly Arjuna took out from his quiver an Anjlika arrow that was effulgent like Indra's thunder-bolt, Agni's rod or the thousand-rayed sun.

verses.sanskrit: मर्मच्छिदं शोणितमांसदिग्धं वैश्वानरार्कप्रतिमं महार्हम् । नराश्वनागासुहरं त्र्यरत्निं षड्वाजमञ्जोगतिमुग्रवेगम् ॥४१॥
verses.english: Capable of cutting to the quick, covered with flesh and blood, effulgent like the sun or fire, made of precious ingredients, straightcoursing, impetuous, destructive of men, horses and elephants it was three cubits and six feet in length. Powerful as the thousand-eyed Indra's thunder-bolt, irresistible as the night rangers, the trident or the discus it was highly terrible and capable of destroying all creatures.

verses.sanskrit: सहस्रनेत्राशनितुल्यवीर्यं कालानलं व्यात्तमिवातिघोरम् । पिनाकनारायणचक्रसन्निभं भयङ्करं प्राणभृतां विनाशनम् ॥४२॥
जग्राह पार्थः स शरं प्रहृष्टो यो देवसङ्घैरपि दुर्निवार्यः । संपूजितो यः सततं महात्मा देवासुरान्यो विजयेन्महेषुः ॥४३॥
verses.english: Partha cheerfully took up that arrow which could not be withstood even by the celestials. This great weapon, capable of discomfiting the celestials and Asuras, was always adored by the son of Pandu.

verses.sanskrit: तं वै प्रमृष्टं प्रसमीक्ष्य युद्धे चचाल सर्वं सचराचरं जगत् । स्वस्ति जगत्स्यादृषयः प्रचुक्रुशुस्तमुद्यतं प्रेक्ष्य महाहवेषुम् ॥४४॥
verses.english: Seeing that arrow taken up by Partha in battle, the entire universe trembled with its mobile and immobile creations. Beholding that arrow about to be discharged the Rishis cried aloud "Peace be to the universe.

verses.sanskrit: ततस्तु तं वै शरमप्रमेयं गाण्डीवधन्वा धनुषि व्ययोजयत् । युक्त्वा महास्त्रेण परेण चापं विकृष्य गाण्डीवमुवाच सत्वरम् ॥४५॥
verses.english: The holder of the Gandiva then set that peerless arrows his bow united with another highly powerful weapon. Then drawing his Gandiva bow he said.

verses.sanskrit: अयं महास्त्रप्रहितो महाशरः शरीरहृच्चासुहरश्च दुर्हृदः । तपोऽस्ति तप्तं गुरवश्च तोषिता मया यदीष्टं सुहृदां श्रुतं तथा ॥४६॥
verses.english: If I have ever practised penances, if I have ever respected my elders and listened to the counsels of well-wishers let this arrow be powerful enough to destroy the body and heart of my enemy. Let his sharp arrow, adored by me, slay my enemy Karna." Saying this Dhananjaya discharged the arrow for destroying Karna.

verses.sanskrit: अनेन सत्येन निहन्त्वयं शरः सुसंश्रितः कर्णमरिं ममोर्जितम् । इत्यूचिवांस्तं प्रमुमोच बाणं धनञ्जयः कर्णवधाय घोरम् ॥४७॥
कृत्यामथर्वाङ्गिरसीमिवोग्रां दीप्तामसह्यां युधि मृत्युनापि । ब्रुवन् किरीटी तमतिप्रहृष्टो ह्ययं शरो मे विजयावहोऽस्तु ॥४८॥
verses.english: It was a terrific arrows, efficacious as a rite of the Atharvan of Angiras, effulgent and incapable of being borne by Death himself in battle. Desirous of slaying Karna Partha again cheerfully said-“May this arrow bring on my victory. May it, effulgent like the fire or sun, shot by me, dispatch Karna to the abode of Death.

verses.sanskrit: जिघांसुरर्केन्दुसमप्रभावः कर्णं मयास्तो नयतां यमाय । तेनेषुवर्येण किरीटमाली प्रहृष्टरूपो विजयावहेन ॥४९॥
verses.english: Saying this, Arjuna, adorned with crown and garlands, ever inimical towards Karna and desirous of killing him, struck his enemy with that best of arrows, effulgent like the sun of moon capable of giving victory.

verses.sanskrit: जिघांसुरर्केन्दुसमप्रभेण चक्रे विषक्तं रिपुमाततायी । तथा विमुक्तो बलिनाऽर्कतेजाः प्रज्वालयामास दिशो नभश्च । ततोऽर्जुनस्तस्य शिरो जहार वृत्रस्य वज्रेण यथा महेन्द्रः ॥५०॥
verses.english: Discharged by that mighty heroic that arrow, effulgent like the sun, emblazoned all the quarters. With that arrow Arjuna struck off his enemy's head like Indra striking the head of Vritra with his thunder.

verses.sanskrit: शरोत्तमेनाञ्जलिकेन राजंस्तदा महास्त्रप्रतिमन्त्रितेन । पार्थोऽपराह्णे शिर उच्चकर्त वैकर्तनस्याथ महेन्द्रसूनुः ॥५१॥
verses.english: With that powerful Anjalika weapon inspired with mantras Indra's son cut-off the head of Vaikartana in the afternoon.

verses.sanskrit: तत्प्रापतच्चाञ्जलिकेन च्छिन्नमपास्य कायो निपपात पश्चात् । तदुद्यतादित्यसमानतेजसं शरन्नभोमध्यगभास्करोपमम् ॥५२॥
verses.english: Thus sundered with Anjalika arrow Karna's trunk dropped down on earth. The head also of the commander of the Kuru army, effulgent like the risen, sun and the meridian sun of the autumn, dropped down on earth like the crimson sun falling down from the setting hill.

verses.sanskrit: वराङ्गमुर्व्यामपतच्चमूमुखे दिवाकरोऽस्तादिव रक्तमण्डलः । ततोऽस्य देहं सततं सुखोचितं सुरूपमत्यर्थमुदारकर्मणः ॥५३॥
verses.english: The head of the illustrious Karna reluctantly left the body, highly beautiful and brought up in luxury like a person unwillingly leaving a big house filled with riches.

verses.sanskrit: परेण कृच्छ्रेण शिरः समत्यजद्गृहं महर्धीव सुसङ्गमीश्वरः । शरैर्विभिन्नं व्यसु तत्सुवर्चसः पपात कर्णस्य शरीरमुच्छ्रितम् ॥५४॥
स्रवद्व्रणं गैरिकतोयविस्रवं गिरेर्यथा वज्रहतं महाशिरः । देहाच्च कर्णस्य निपातितस्य तेजः सूर्यं खं वितत्याविवेश ॥५५॥
verses.english: Cut-off with Arjuna's arrows and shorn of life the tall and shining body of Karna, with blood gushing out of every wound, looked like the summit of a red chalk mount clapped by a thunder-bolt with red streams running down after a shower. Then a light came out of Karna's body, passed though the sky and entered into the sun.

verses.sanskrit: तद‌द्भुतं सर्वमनुष्ययोधाः संदृष्टवन्तो निहते स्म कर्णे । ततः शङ्खान् पाण्डवा दध्मुरुच्चैर्दृष्ट्वा कर्णं पातितं फाल्गुनेन ॥५६॥
verses.english: This wonderful spectacle was wiinessed by all the on-lookers after Karna's fall. Then seeing Karna slain by Phalguna the Pandavas blew their conchs.

verses.sanskrit: तथैव कृष्णश्च धनञ्जयश्च हृष्टौ यमौ दध्मतुर्वारिजातौ । तं सोमकाः प्रेक्ष्य हतं शयानं सैन्यैः सार्धं सिंहनादान्प्रचकुः ॥५७॥
verses.english: Likewise Krishna and Dhananjaya, overflowing with joy, blew their conchs. Seeing Karna slain and lying on the battle-field the Somakas were filled the joy and sent-up loud shouts with other soldiers.

verses.sanskrit: तूर्याणि सञ्जघ्नुरतीव हृष्टा वासांसि चैवादुधुवुर्भुजांश्च । संवर्धयन्तश्च नरेन्द्रयोधाः पार्थं समाजग्मुरतीव हृष्टाः ॥५८॥
verses.english: With great joy the struck their trumphets and shook their arms and garments. Then, O king, approaching Partha, all the warriors began to praise him; other powerful heroes danced embracing each other; and others sending loud shouts said-"By good luck Karna has slain prostrate on earth wounded with arrows."

verses.sanskrit: बलान्विताश्चापरे ह्यप्यनृत्यन्नन्योन्यमाश्लिष्य नदन्त ऊचुः । दृष्ट्वा तु कर्णं भुवि वा विपन्नं कृत्तं रथात्सायकैरर्जुनस्य ॥५९॥
महानिलेनाद्रिमिवापविद्धं यज्ञावसानेऽग्निमिव प्रशान्तम् । रराज कर्णस्य शिरो निकृत्तमस्तं गतं भास्करस्येव बिम्बम् ॥६०॥
verses.english: Karna's head, separated off the body, looked like a mountain top loosened by a storm or like fire put out after the completion of a sacrifice, or the sun after it has risen the setting hill.

verses.sanskrit: शरैराचितसर्वाङ्गः शोणितौघपरिप्लुतः । विभाति देहः कर्णस्य स्वरश्मिभिरिवांशुमान् ॥६१॥
verses.english: Karna's body filled with all parts arrow penetrated and soaked in blood was getting the grace of sun, the holder of beams and illuminated.

verses.sanskrit: प्रताप्य सेनामामित्रीं दीप्तैः शरगभस्तिभिः । बलिनाऽर्जुनकालेन नीतोऽस्तं कर्णभास्करः ॥६२॥
verses.english: After having scorched his enemy's army the Karna-like sun, having arrows for its rays, was caused to be set by Arjuna time.

verses.sanskrit: अस्तं गच्छन्यथादित्यः प्रभामादाय गच्छति । तथा जीवितमादाय कर्णस्येषुर्जगाम सः । अपराह्णेऽपराह्णोऽस्य सूतपुत्रस्य मारिष ॥६३॥
verses.english: As while moving towards the setting hill the sun withdraws all its rays so (Arjuna's) arrow passed of taking Karna's vital breaths.

verses.sanskrit: छिन्नमञ्जलिकेनाजौ सोत्सेधमपतच्छिरः । उपर्युपरि सैन्यानामस्य शत्रोस्तदञ्जसा । शिरः कर्णस्य सोत्सेधमिषुः सोऽप्यहरद्द्रुतम् ॥६४॥
verses.english: Before the very presence of the Kaurava troops that weapon speedily took away Karna's head and body.
verses.bhavadeepa: अपराह्णे दिवसस्य पश्चिमे भागे अपरं चरमम् अहः मरणदिनं यस्य ॥६३॥

verses.sanskrit: कर्णं तु शूरं पतितं पृथिव्यां शराचितं शोणितदिग्धगात्रम् । दृष्ट्वा शयानं भुवि मद्रराजश्छिन्नध्वजेनाथ ययौ रथेन ॥६५॥
verses.english: Beholding the brave Karna prostrated on earth wounded with shafts and bathed in blood the king of Madras left the battle field on the car deprived of the standard.

verses.sanskrit: हते कर्णे कुरवः प्राद्रवन्त भयार्दिता गाढविद्धाश्च संख्ये । अवेक्षमाणा मुहुरर्जुनस्य ध्वजं महान्तं वपुषा ज्वलन्तम् ॥६६॥
verses.english: After Karna's fall the Kuru soldiers, wounded with arrows and filled with fear, took to their heels looking again and again on the lofty and shining standard of Arjuna.

verses.sanskrit: सहस्रनेत्रप्रतिमानकर्मणः सहस्रपत्रप्रतिमाननं शुभम् । सहस्ररश्मिर्दिनसंक्षये यथा तथाऽपतत्कर्णशिरो वसुन्धराम् ॥६७॥
verses.english: The beautiful head, having a countenance like a loutus of a thousand petals, of Karna, whose exploits like those of the thousand eyes Indra, drooped down on earth like the thousand-rayed sun in the end of day.
